name: זִמְרִי
summary: Borne by Zimri son of Salu, a chief of Simeon, struck down by Phinehas with the Midianite woman at Peor (Num 25:14); by Zimri the chariot commander who killed Elah and reigned seven days in Tirzah before burning the king's house over himself, so that Jezebel taunted Jehu as a “Zimri, murderer of his master” (1Ki 16:9–20; 2Ki 9:31); by a son of Zerah of Judah (1Ch 2:6), called Zabdi in Jos 7:1; and by a Benjamite of Saul's line (1Ch 8:36; 9:42). The name is the root's זמר with the ending ִי; read with זִמְרָה “song” it is “my song”, and with an older ḏmr “protection”, “my protection”. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The name of the man of Israel who was struck … was זִמְרִי son of Salu, a chief of a father's house of the Simeonites.”
“His servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him … and reigned in his place.”
Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah and burned the king's house over himself.
“Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?”
“The sons of Zerah: זִמְרִי and Ethan and Heman and Calcol and Dara.”
Achan “son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah”: the same man as Zimri of 1Ch 2:6.
“Yah is my strength and my זִמְרָת”: the noun the name is read from.

note: Takes g.bs.ad only; g.bs.ae is BDB's gentilic for Jer 25:25 “the kings of Zimri”, a people or place (TIPNR Zimri@Jer.25.25 is a place), left out. TIPNR files the Zimri of 1Ch 2:6 under Zabdi@Jos.7.1, whose forms include זִמְרִי; tagged here. The meaning “my song” or “my protection” is a reading of the form only (see the entry's note on ḏmr and Amorite names in zimri-).
